findings.title: Rule 16's operator action prescribes a re-drive of a terminally failed purge that no code path can perform
findings.reason: Round 2 re-resolved every clause of the replacement paragraph against 4070fad. 'validatePurgeableOffboarding rejects the row (account_offboarding_status_not_purgeable:failed)' - purge-stages.ts:92-94 returns `account_offboarding_status_not_purgeable:${row.status}` for any status other than purge_scheduled, and markPurgeTerminalFailure (purge-stages.ts:1236-1238) leaves status='failed'. 'AccountOffboardingPurgePoller claims only status=purge_scheduled AND purge_started_at IS NULL' - poller lines 103+121 (claim SELECT) and 155+173 (claim UPDATE). 'the teardown retry path is scoped to failed_step=teardown' - AccountOffboardingTeardownRetryPoller:91-92,112-113 and shouldTransitionToPurgeScheduled (provider-disposition.ts:281-282). 'no admin route mutates purge state' - no UPDATE account_offboardings under src/app; the two library writers are reactivate.ts (status='scheduled' only) and keep-my-data.ts (status IN pending/tearing_down/purge_scheduled AND purge_started_at IS NULL), neither reachable for a failed purge. 'failed_step=purge is a CONSTANT' - purge-stages.ts:1238 writes the literal. 'Stripe Customer redaction first ... before runParentTombstonePurgeStage leaves names, emails, phones and addresses while the auth user is already deleted' - PurgeWorker.ts:133-141 runs redaction (1), auth binding (2) ... parent tombstone (9), and the tombstone stage is where name/email/phone/address/owner_* are sentinelled (purge-stages.ts:928-957). 'There is no per-stage checkpoint - the handler replays from stage 1' - the nine stage calls are unconditional. The claim 'tracked in #1411' is UNVERIFIABLE-EXTERNAL (no network in this pass), not false.

findings.title: The runbook doc-pin still passes when the rule row's two fingerprint spellings are SWAPPED: the assertions are regexes over the whole row, not over the cell that owns the value
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured survivor M6 on inventory row RT-A6. The fix narrowed the pin from file-wide to rule-16's block and row, which kills every corruption round 1 found (M1-M5, M6b, M6c all failed). It does not close the class, because the SAME row carries both spellings: the grouping cell states the terminal fingerprint and a later sentence in that cell states the retry fingerprint. Swapping them leaves `expect(row).toMatch(fingerprintPattern([...PREFIX,'<account_offboarding_id>']))` matching the retry-arm sentence and `expect(block).toMatch(fingerprintPattern(PURGE_RETRY_FINGERPRINT))` matching the grouping cell. Not equivalent: after the mutation the operator's 'custom fingerprint' cell - the one value they paste into Sentry's grouping override - reads [account_offboarding_purge_failed, retry], so the configured rule groups on the retry issue and is silent for the terminal event. That is exactly the RT-08 failure this change exists to close, and it is the same failure mode round 1 reported, one scope level down. Not an unexecuted branch: the test reads the row at :941 and every assertion runs. Behavioural replacement: assert on the fingerprint's POSITION, not its presence - e.g. split the 'Level and grouping' cell at 'custom fingerprint' and require the terminal pattern in the head of that cell, and require the retry pattern only after the words 'The retry arm takes'. Or, cheaper and sufficient: assert the grouping cell's first fingerprint occurrence equals the terminal spelling.

findings.title: The arch-review ledger asserts present-tense rule-1 coverage for a rule that is not configured and whose trigger is first-seen
findings.reason: The ledger paragraph was rewritten and each replacement clause re-resolves TRUE at 4070fad. 'rule 1 is unconfigured' - its section-1 checklist box is `- [ ]` at beta-launch-alerting.md:56. 'triggers on first-seen' - the rule table row 1 at :435 reads 'issue is first seen'. 'over an unfingerprinted count-bearing message' - health-alert/emit.ts:12 calls Sentry.captureMessage(finding.title, ...) with tags and extra but NO fingerprint, and checks.ts:132 builds the title as `${count} ${topic} job(s) exhausted retries and failed in the last ${window}s`. 'the finding never carries the offboarding id' - checks.ts:133 detail is {topic, count, window_s}. 'it would fire once per distinct count, not per failure' follows from those two. The runbook's matching paragraph at :582 states the same facts, including HEALTH_ALERT_FAILED_THRESHOLD default 0 (checks.ts:78).

findings.title: stripCommentLines opened a false-negative hole: a CODE line whose trimmed form starts with `*` is stripped, so a key respelling there is invisible to the guard
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured: M15 inserted `const F = (b: string): number => 1\n  * \`csv_ingest_${b}\`.length;` into worker/jobs/account-offboarding/purge-stages.ts; the single-owner test stayed GREEN, while the same respelling on an ordinary line (M14) turned it red. The filter at :107 drops any line whose trimStart() begins with `*`, which is a multiplication continuation as well as a JSDoc body line. This is a genuine regression in guard strength relative to the merge base, where the scan read raw source and would have matched. Recorded P2, not P0, and this is a deliberate deviation from the skill's survivor->P0 mapping, stated so it can be overruled: a `*`-leading source line is not a shape production key construction takes, the mutant is contrived, and the test's own comment already declares the guard is 'a regex over source text, not a dataflow analysis ... not a proof of single ownership'. Cheap hardening if wanted: strip only `//`, `/*` and ` * ` (space-star-space) rather than bare `*`.

findings.title: Rule 16's row states the event level twice and the pin covers only one of them
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured: M3b inverted the grouping cell's leading level token (| `error`; custom fingerprint -> | `warning`; custom fingerprint) at beta-launch-alerting.md:576 and the test stayed GREEN, because the only level assertion is /level\s+equals\s+`error`/ against the FILTER cell. The mutated row is internally contradictory - it filters on level error while declaring the terminal event is warning - and contradicts PurgeWorker.ts:172. P2 rather than P0 (the same deliberate deviation stated in RT16-09): the filter cell is the value the operator pastes into Sentry, the grouping cell's token is a descriptive restatement, and the level facet does remain pinned in the same row. Behavioural replacement: assert the grouping cell opens with the same level the filter cell requires.
